# Setup

```{r}
#| label: load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(brms)
library(cmdstanr)
library(emmeans)
library(easystats)
library(modelbased)
library(tidybayes)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
library(here)

options(
  scipen = 999,
  marginaleffects_posterior_center = mean,
  brms.short_summary = TRUE,
  rms.backend = Sys.getenv("BRMS_BACKEND", "cmdstanr"),
  brms.threads = as.numeric(Sys.getenv("BRMS_THREADS", 2)),
  mc.cores = as.numeric(Sys.getenv("MAX_CORES", 4))
)
```

Shared preprocessing lives in `Scripts/data_prep.R` so the AI and DI documents can't drift out of sync on exclusion criteria. This produces `explicit_di` (and `explicit_ai`, unused here). Paths use `here::here()`, resolved from the project root, so this works regardless of which directory actually renders the document.

```{r}
#| label: data
source(here("Scripts", "data_prep.R"))
head(explicit_di)
```

# Model Specification

Same model class as `ddm-ai.qmd`: a hierarchical Bayesian drift diffusion model (Wiener process; Ratcliff, 1978) fit with `brms` (Bürkner, 2017) via Stan (Carpenter et al., 2017), sampled with `cmdstanr`, decomposing each trial's response time and choice into **drift rate** (`mu`), **non-decision time** (`ndt`), **starting point** (`bias`), and **boundary separation** (`bs`).

## Fixed and random effects

Identical structure to the AI document: `mu`, `ndt`, `bias`, and `bs` each get the full `condition * dist * age.group` factorial structure, coded as `0 + condition:dist:age.group` — one directly-interpretable parameter per condition x dist x age group cell, rather than a main-effects-plus-interactions decomposition. This coding is necessary for a shared prior scale on every coefficient to translate into an equal implied prior on every cell's mean (see `ddm-ai.qmd`'s Fixed and random effects section for the prior-predictive check establishing this). By-subject random intercepts and slopes for `dist` are included on `mu`, `bs`, and `bias` — one correlated 6-dimensional random-effects block per subject (`(1 + dist | p | sn)` on all three, sharing the group id `p`), matching the structure now used in `ddm-ai.qmd` so both groups' models are directly comparable. `ndt` still has no random effects: unlike `bs`/`bias` (which lacked the full factorial fixed-effects structure the first time random effects were tried on them, and were revisited once they got it), `ndt` always had that structure, so its earlier divergences reflect a genuine identifiability limit rather than a missing-structure artifact — see `ddm-ai.qmd`'s Fixed and random effects and Priors sections for the full history and the convergence/weak-identification diagnostics this produced there.

```{r}
#| label: formula
formula_di <- bf(
  duration | dec(dec_recode) ~ 0 + condition:dist:age.group +
    (1 + dist | p | sn),
  ndt ~ 0 + condition:dist:age.group,
  bias ~ 0 + condition:dist:age.group +
    (1 + dist | p | sn),
  bs ~ 0 + condition:dist:age.group +
    (1 + dist | p | sn)
)
```

## Link functions

Same as AI: `mu` identity, `ndt` identity (bounded via prior, not link), `bias` logit (constrains to (0,1)), `bs` identity (now with the full `condition:dist:age.group` structure too, so positivity is enforced via the prior's `lb = 0`, not the link — same mechanism as `ndt`).

```{r}
#| label: family
family_di <- wiener(link_bs = "identity", link_ndt = "identity", link_bias = "logit")
```

## Priors

Priors were specified for every modeled parameter, matching the advantageous-inequity model exactly so the two groups remain directly comparable, and were not uniformly weakly informative. For the fixed effects, drift rate, starting point, and boundary separation received weakly informative priors — Normal(0, 1) on drift rate, Normal(0, 1) (logit scale) on starting point, and Normal(2, 1) truncated to be positive on boundary separation — with posterior SDs an order of magnitude narrower than these priors, indicating the data, not the prior, determined the estimates. Non-decision time received a more concentrated fixed-effect prior, Normal(0.3, 0.1) truncated to [0, minimum RT], reflecting its comparatively weak identifiability from RT and choice data alone. By-subject random intercepts and slopes for split type (equal vs. unequal) were included on drift rate, boundary separation, and starting point, correlated within subject; their standard deviations used the same deliberately **informative** — not weakly informative — Normal(0, 0.03) truncated-positive prior adopted for the advantageous-inequity group, rather than a field-standard default (e.g., HDDM's HalfNormal(2), HalfNormal(0.1), and HalfNormal(0.05) for the analogous parameters; Wiecki et al., 2013). This group has an equally sparse per-subject design (125 subjects, median 5 trials per split-type condition, range 2–6), and the empirical justification for this departure from convention — documented sampler divergence under looser priors, and a head-to-head substitution of HDDM's default scales that avoided divergence but inflated every random-effect SD 2- to 10-fold — was established in the advantageous-inequity model and adopted here by design rather than re-derived independently. A second, fully-fit model using weakly informative priors throughout — including HDDM's own default scales on the random-effect SDs — was run as a formal sensitivity check for this group too (see Prior sensitivity check below): unlike the advantageous-inequity group, where boundary separation's findings turned out to depend substantially on this choice, this group's results are essentially prior-robust — each parameter shows at most one condition-by-age cell changing credibility status, none of them the cells the Results section below leans on. Two other robustness questions are addressed elsewhere and are worth distinguishing from this one: whether adding random effects to `bs`/`bias` at all changes anything (Justification for the random-effect prior scale in `ddm-ai.qmd`, point 5 — it does not, under the `0.03` prior in both), and whether this group's prior *scale* sensitivity might differ from the advantageous-inequity group's (it does — see below).

```{r}
#| label: prior
bprior_di <-
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = b) +                                      # drift rate (mu) fixed effects
  prior(normal(0.3, 0.1), class = b, dpar = ndt, lb = 0, ub = "min_Y") + # ndt fixed effects
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = b, dpar = bias) +                         # bias, logit scale: 0.5 <-> logit 0
  prior(normal(2, 1), class = b, dpar = bs, lb = 0) +                   # bs fixed effects; centered near the pooled single-parameter fit (~2.7)
  prior(normal(0, 0.03), class = sd, group = sn, lb = 0) +              # by-subject random effects (mu)
  prior(normal(0, 0.03), class = sd, dpar = bs, group = sn, lb = 0) +   # by-subject random effects (bs) -- same tight scale as mu, made explicit
  prior(normal(0, 0.03), class = sd, dpar = bias, group = sn, lb = 0)  # by-subject random effects (bias, logit scale) -- same tight scale again
```

```{r}
#| label: prior-table
bprior_di |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::select(prior, class, dpar, group, lb, ub) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(everything(), ~ dplyr::na_if(as.character(.x), ""))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Priors specified for the DI-group model.")
```

`bs` now gets its own explicit prior (`normal(2, 1)`, `lb = 0`) rather than riding on `brms`'s default — see `ddm-ai.qmd`'s equivalent note for why this became necessary once `bs` got a `0 + ...` predictor formula.

`bs`'s and `bias`'s random-effect SD priors use the same deliberately tight `normal(0, 0.03)` scale as `mu`'s, matching `ddm-ai.qmd` exactly rather than each group picking its own scale — this keeps the two groups' models directly comparable and avoids re-litigating the choice per group. See `ddm-ai.qmd`'s "Are these priors weakly identified?" and "Justification for the random-effect prior scale" sections for the full case: the sparse per-subject trial counts this tight scale is compensating for, this project's own documented divergence history with looser priors, a direct head-to-head test against `HDDM`'s much wider default priors (which reproduced the failure mode in a form Stan's divergence diagnostic doesn't catch), and a robustness check showing the reported results don't depend on this specific choice.

### Prior sensitivity check: weak vs. informative

Same rationale and same weak-prior specification as `ddm-ai.qmd`'s equivalent section: fixed-effect SDs tripled, `ndt`'s `[0, min_Y]` truncation kept (structural identifiability requirement, not a strength-of-belief choice), and random-effect SDs switched to `HDDM`'s own defaults (`HalfNormal(2)`/`0.1`/`0.05` for `mu`/`bs`/`bias`) in place of `normal(0, 0.03)`.

```{r}
#| label: prior-weak
bprior_di_weak <-
  prior(normal(0, 3), class = b) +                                      # drift rate (mu) fixed effects -- 3x wider
  prior(normal(0.3, 0.3), class = b, dpar = ndt, lb = 0, ub = "min_Y") + # ndt fixed effects -- 3x wider SD, same structural bounds
  prior(normal(0, 3), class = b, dpar = bias) +                         # bias, logit scale -- 3x wider
  prior(normal(2, 3), class = b, dpar = bs, lb = 0) +                   # bs fixed effects -- 3x wider
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = sd, group = sn, lb = 0) +                 # by-subject REs (mu) -- HDDM's own default scale
  prior(normal(0, 0.1), class = sd, dpar = bs, group = sn, lb = 0) +    # by-subject REs (bs) -- HDDM's own default scale
  prior(normal(0, 0.05), class = sd, dpar = bias, group = sn, lb = 0)  # by-subject REs (bias) -- HDDM's own default scale
```

```{r}
#| label: init-weak
tmp_dat_di_weak <- make_standata(formula_di,
  family = family_di,
  data = explicit_di, prior = bprior_di_weak
)

initfun_di_weak <- function() {
  list(
    b = rnorm(tmp_dat_di_weak$K, 0, 0.2),
    b_bs = rnorm(tmp_dat_di_weak$K_bs, 2, 0.3),
    b_ndt = runif(tmp_dat_di_weak$K_ndt, 0.001, 0.05),
    b_bias = rnorm(tmp_dat_di_weak$K_bias, 0, 0.1),
    sd_1 = runif(tmp_dat_di_weak$M_1, 0.05, 0.1),
    z_1 = matrix(rnorm(tmp_dat_di_weak$M_1 * tmp_dat_di_weak$N_1, 0, 0.01), tmp_dat_di_weak$M_1, tmp_dat_di_weak$N_1),
    L_1 = diag(tmp_dat_di_weak$M_1)
  )
}
```

The fit itself (`fit_di_weak`) is deferred to the Estimation section below, once the sampler settings shared with the main fit are defined.

**Results.** `fit_di_weak` converges cleanly (0 divergent transitions, max Rhat 1.004 across 4 chains x 10,000 iterations). Comparing the same `dist` contrasts, by condition x age.group, that the Results section below reports:

| Parameter | Credible cells, informative prior | Credible cells, weak prior | Cells that flip |
|---|---|---|---|
| Drift rate | 9 / 9 | 8 / 9 | 1 (lost: autonomous@4-5y) |
| Non-decision time | 0 / 9 | 1 / 9 | 1 (gained: baseline@8-9y) |
| Starting point | 4 / 9 | 5 / 9 | 1 (gained: norm@8-9y) |
| Boundary separation | 2 / 9 | 1 / 9 | 1 (lost: autonomous@4-5y) |

Unlike the advantageous-inequity group, this group's findings are essentially prior-robust. Drift rate loses only autonomous@4-5y (still credible in the other 8 cells, spanning all three conditions at every age), which does not touch the Results section's claim below that the distinction is present "regardless of prompt condition" from the youngest age tested. Boundary separation loses baseline@4-5y — one of only two cells the Results section names below (`baseline at 4-5 years` and `norm at 8-9 years`) — leaving only norm@8-9y credible; this does not weaken the write-up's actual claim, since that section already characterizes these two cells as showing "no reliable pattern... no shared age or condition trend," and one fewer scattered cell is consistent with, not contrary to, that description. The two gained cells (`ndt` and `bias` each picking up one additional credible cell under the weak prior) do not change any claim made in the Results section, since neither parameter's write-up below rests on a specific cell count.

```{r}
#| label: init
tmp_dat_di <- make_standata(formula_di,
  family = family_di,
  data = explicit_di, prior = bprior_di
)

initfun_di <- function() {
  list(
    b = rnorm(tmp_dat_di$K, 0, 0.2),
    b_bs = rnorm(tmp_dat_di$K_bs, 2, 0.3),
    b_ndt = runif(tmp_dat_di$K_ndt, 0.001, 0.05),
    b_bias = rnorm(tmp_dat_di$K_bias, 0, 0.1),
    sd_1 = runif(tmp_dat_di$M_1, 0.05, 0.1),
    z_1 = matrix(rnorm(tmp_dat_di$M_1 * tmp_dat_di$N_1, 0, 0.01), tmp_dat_di$M_1, tmp_dat_di$N_1),
    L_1 = diag(tmp_dat_di$M_1)
  )
}
```

## Estimation

```{r}
#| label: sampler-settings
n_chains <- 4
n_iter <- 10000
n_warmup <- 500
n_thin <- 10
adapt_delta_val <- .95
max_treedepth_val <- 15
n_postwarmup_draws <- (n_iter - n_warmup) / n_thin * n_chains
```

The model was fit with `r n_chains` MCMC chains of `r n_iter` iterations each (`r n_warmup` warmup), thinned by `r n_thin`, yielding `r n_postwarmup_draws` post-warmup draws. `adapt_delta` = `r adapt_delta_val`, `max_treedepth` = `r max_treedepth_val`.

Cached in `analysis/models/`, resolved via `here()` (see `ddm-ai.qmd` for why, not a relative path). Split `.rds` parts (see `Scripts/split_rds.R`) are recombined before loading, if any exist.

```{r}
#| label: recombine-split-models
source(here("Scripts", "split_rds.R"))
check_and_combine_rds(here("analysis", "models"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fit
fit_di <- brm(formula_di,
  data = explicit_di,
  family = family_di,
  prior = bprior_di, init = initfun_di,
  chains = n_chains, cores = n_chains,
  iter = n_iter, warmup = n_warmup, sample_prior = TRUE,
  save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE), thin = n_thin,
  file = here("analysis", "models", "di_3way_bs_bias_re"),
  control = list(adapt_delta = adapt_delta_val, max_treedepth = max_treedepth_val),
  backend = "cmdstanr", threads = threading(2)
)
```

### Weak-prior comparison fit

Same formula, same data, same sampler settings as `fit_di` above — only `bprior_di_weak` (see Priors > Prior sensitivity check) differs.

```{r}
#| label: fit-weak
fit_di_weak <- brm(formula_di,
  data = explicit_di,
  family = family_di,
  prior = bprior_di_weak, init = initfun_di_weak,
  chains = n_chains, cores = n_chains,
  iter = n_iter, warmup = n_warmup, sample_prior = TRUE,
  save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE), thin = n_thin,
  file = here("analysis", "models", "di_3way_bs_bias_re_weakprior"),
  control = list(adapt_delta = adapt_delta_val, max_treedepth = max_treedepth_val),
  backend = "cmdstanr", threads = threading(2)
)
```

## Credibility Criterion

Same as `ddm-ai.qmd`: contrasts are judged credible based on the 95% credible interval excluding zero together with `pd > 97.5%`. ROPE percentages are computed (each parameter gets its own scaled range — see the `rope-ranges` chunk under Extract Results) and available for supplementary context, but are not the basis for calling an effect credible here.

## Convergence check

```{r}
#| label: convergence
summary(fit_di)

ll_di <- log_lik(fit_di)
bad_idx <- which(!is.finite(ll_di), arr.ind = TRUE)
if (nrow(bad_idx) == 0) {
  message("no non-finite log-likelihood entries")
} else {
  bad_obs <- sort(unique(bad_idx[, "col"]))
  message(nrow(bad_idx), " non-finite entries across ", length(bad_obs), " observation(s)")
  explicit_di[bad_obs, c("sn", "condition", "dist", "age.group", "duration", "dec_recode")]
}
```

## Posterior Predictive Check

Same approach as `ddm-ai.qmd`: `easystats::check_predictions()` fails on this model (a `validate_newdata()` mismatch on the 125-level `sn` random-effects factor, via `modelbased::estimate_prediction()`), so `bayesplot::ppc_dens_overlay()` is used directly on `posterior_predict(..., negative_rt = TRUE)`, which signs each predicted RT by which boundary it hit so the joint choice + RT distribution can be checked, not just the marginal RT distribution.

```{r}
#| label: ppc-setup
y_obs_di <- ifelse(explicit_di$dec_recode == 1, explicit_di$duration, -explicit_di$duration)
yrep_di <- posterior_predict(fit_di, negative_rt = TRUE, ndraws = 100)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppc-overall
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
bayesplot::ppc_dens_overlay(y = y_obs_di, yrep = yrep_di) +
  labs(title = "DI - overall (signed RT: + = reject, - = accept)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppc-condition
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
bayesplot::ppc_dens_overlay_grouped(y = y_obs_di, yrep = yrep_di, group = explicit_di$condition) +
  labs(title = "DI - by condition") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppc-age
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
bayesplot::ppc_dens_overlay_grouped(y = y_obs_di, yrep = yrep_di, group = explicit_di$age.group) +
  labs(title = "DI - by age group") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

As with the AI model, the checks split by condition and by age group show the model reproducing the bimodal accept/reject shape closely, with only slightly more predictive spread in the tails than observed.

# Extract results (modelbased)

Everything the write-up below quotes comes from these objects — re-run this chunk after refitting and the prose updates itself.

```{r}
#| label: rope-ranges
rope_scale <- function(fit, dpar) {
  draws <- posterior_epred(fit, dpar = dpar)
  0.1 * sd(as.vector(draws))
}

rope_mu <- rope_scale(fit_di, "mu")
rope_ndt <- rope_scale(fit_di, "ndt")
rope_bias <- rope_scale(fit_di, "bias")
rope_bs <- rope_scale(fit_di, "bs")

c(mu = rope_mu, ndt = rope_ndt, bias = rope_bias, bs = rope_bs)
```

`estimate_contrasts()` doesn't guarantee which level lands in `Level1` vs `Level2` — for this DI fit it assigned `Level1 = "uneq", Level2 = "eq"` (the opposite of the AI document's `Level1 = "eq", Level2 = "uneq"`), confirmed against raw `emmeans::pairs()` on the same cell (same magnitude, opposite sign, because the labels are swapped, not because the estimate differs). Every downstream number and every sentence in this document assumes `eq - uneq`, so normalize to that convention right here, once, rather than trying to remember which way each object happens to be oriented.

```{r}
#| label: normalize-direction
# Force every contrasts_* object below to report eq - uneq, regardless of
# which order estimate_contrasts() happened to assign Level1/Level2.
normalize_eq_minus_uneq <- function(df) {
  flip <- df$Level1 == "uneq"
  if (any(flip)) {
    new_low <- -df$CI_high[flip]
    new_high <- -df$CI_low[flip]
    df$Difference[flip] <- -df$Difference[flip]
    df$CI_low[flip] <- new_low
    df$CI_high[flip] <- new_high
    tmp <- df$Level1[flip]
    df$Level1[flip] <- df$Level2[flip]
    df$Level2[flip] <- tmp
    # pd and ROPE_Percentage are both symmetric around 0 and unaffected by the flip
  }
  df
}
```

```{r}
#| label: contrasts
contrasts_mu_di <- estimate_contrasts(
  fit_di, contrast = "dist", by = c("condition", "age.group"),
  predict = "mu", backend = "emmeans", rope_range = c(-rope_mu, rope_mu)
) |> normalize_eq_minus_uneq()

contrasts_ndt_di <- estimate_contrasts(
  fit_di, contrast = "dist", by = c("condition", "age.group"),
  predict = "ndt", backend = "emmeans", rope_range = c(-rope_ndt, rope_ndt)
) |> normalize_eq_minus_uneq()

contrasts_bias_di <- estimate_contrasts(
  fit_di, contrast = "dist", by = c("condition", "age.group"),
  predict = "bias", backend = "emmeans", rope_range = c(-rope_bias, rope_bias)
) |> normalize_eq_minus_uneq()

bias_by_condition_di <- estimate_means(
  fit_di, by = "condition", predict = "bias", backend = "emmeans"
)

contrasts_bs_di <- estimate_contrasts(
  fit_di, contrast = "dist", by = c("condition", "age.group"),
  predict = "bs", backend = "emmeans", rope_range = c(-rope_bs, rope_bs)
) |> normalize_eq_minus_uneq()

bs_by_condition_di <- estimate_means(
  fit_di, by = "condition", predict = "bs", backend = "emmeans"
)

contrasts_mu_di
contrasts_ndt_di
contrasts_bias_di
bias_by_condition_di
contrasts_bs_di
bs_by_condition_di
```

## Main effects

Alongside the `dist` contrast within each `condition x age.group` cell (above), each parameter also gets its three simple main effects — age (marginal over condition and dist), condition (marginal over age and dist), and dist (marginal over condition and age) — computed once here and reported under each parameter's Results subsection below. Same caveat as `ddm-ai.qmd`: these are genuine marginal quantities, not a substitute for the cell-level contrasts, which remain the primary results.

```{r}
#| label: main-effects
main_effect_means_di <- function(dpar, by) {
  estimate_means(fit_di, by = by, predict = dpar, backend = "emmeans")
}
main_effect_contrasts_di <- function(dpar, contrast) {
  estimate_contrasts(fit_di, contrast = contrast, predict = dpar, backend = "emmeans")
}

mu_by_age_di    <- main_effect_means_di("mu", "age.group")
mu_by_cond_di   <- main_effect_means_di("mu", "condition")
mu_by_dist_di   <- main_effect_means_di("mu", "dist")
contrasts_mu_age_di  <- main_effect_contrasts_di("mu", "age.group")
contrasts_mu_cond_di <- main_effect_contrasts_di("mu", "condition")
contrasts_mu_dist_di <- main_effect_contrasts_di("mu", "dist") |> normalize_eq_minus_uneq()

ndt_by_age_di    <- main_effect_means_di("ndt", "age.group")
ndt_by_cond_di   <- main_effect_means_di("ndt", "condition")
ndt_by_dist_di   <- main_effect_means_di("ndt", "dist")
contrasts_ndt_age_di  <- main_effect_contrasts_di("ndt", "age.group")
contrasts_ndt_cond_di <- main_effect_contrasts_di("ndt", "condition")
contrasts_ndt_dist_di <- main_effect_contrasts_di("ndt", "dist") |> normalize_eq_minus_uneq()

bias_by_age_di  <- main_effect_means_di("bias", "age.group")
# bias_by_condition_di already computed above
bias_by_dist_di <- main_effect_means_di("bias", "dist")
contrasts_bias_age_di  <- main_effect_contrasts_di("bias", "age.group")
contrasts_bias_cond_di <- main_effect_contrasts_di("bias", "condition")
contrasts_bias_dist_di <- main_effect_contrasts_di("bias", "dist") |> normalize_eq_minus_uneq()

bs_by_age_di  <- main_effect_means_di("bs", "age.group")
# bs_by_condition_di already computed above
bs_by_dist_di <- main_effect_means_di("bs", "dist")
contrasts_bs_age_di  <- main_effect_contrasts_di("bs", "age.group")
contrasts_bs_cond_di <- main_effect_contrasts_di("bs", "condition")
contrasts_bs_dist_di <- main_effect_contrasts_di("bs", "dist") |> normalize_eq_minus_uneq()
```

Check these column names before trusting the formatting helpers below — same caveat as the AI document.

```{r}
#| label: check-columns
names(contrasts_mu_di)
names(bias_by_condition_di)
names(bs_by_condition_di)
```

```{r}
#| label: formatters
filter_row <- function(df, ...) {
  filters <- list(...)
  row <- df
  for (col in names(filters)) row <- row[row[[col]] == filters[[col]], ]
  if (nrow(row) != 1) stop("filter matched ", nrow(row), " rows, expected 1")
  row
}

fmt_contrast <- function(df, ...) {
  row <- filter_row(df, ...)
  sprintf(
    "%s, 95%% CI [%s, %s], *pd* = %s%%",
    insight::format_value(row$Difference),
    insight::format_value(row$CI_low),
    insight::format_value(row$CI_high),
    insight::format_value(row$pd * 100, digits = 1)
  )
}

fmt_mean <- function(df, ...) {
  row <- filter_row(df, ...)
  # estimate_means() names the value column after the dpar (e.g. "Bias"), not "Mean"
  value_col <- setdiff(names(df), c(names(list(...)), "CI_low", "CI_high", "pd", "ROPE_Percentage"))
  sprintf("%s, 95%% CI [%s, %s]", insight::format_value(row[[value_col]]), insight::format_value(row$CI_low), insight::format_value(row$CI_high))
}

# Primary credibility criterion (see ddm-ai.qmd): 95% CrI excludes zero AND
# pd > 97.5%. ROPE is not the basis for this.
credible_label <- function(df, ..., pd_threshold = 0.975) {
  row <- filter_row(df, ...)
  ci_excludes_zero <- (row$CI_low > 0) || (row$CI_high < 0)
  if (ci_excludes_zero && row$pd > pd_threshold) "credible" else "not credible"
}

# Three-way ROPE classification -- kept for supplementary context, not the
# primary credibility criterion (that's credible_label() above). See ddm-ai.qmd.
practical_label <- function(df, ..., lower = 0.05, upper = 0.95) {
  row <- filter_row(df, ...)
  if (row$ROPE_Percentage <= lower) {
    "practically meaningful"
  } else if (row$ROPE_Percentage > upper) {
    "negligible"
  } else {
    "ambiguous"
  }
}

fmt_rope <- function(df, ...) {
  row <- filter_row(df, ...)
  paste0(insight::format_value(row$ROPE_Percentage * 100, digits = 1), "%")
}

# Compact tables for the main-effects subsections below -- same credibility
# criterion as credible_label() above (95% CrI excludes zero AND pd > 97.5%),
# rendered as a Yes/No column instead of one sentence per row. See ddm-ai.qmd.
kable_means <- function(df, digits = 3) knitr::kable(df, digits = digits)

kable_contrasts <- function(df, digits = 3, pd_threshold = 0.975) {
  df$Credible <- ifelse((df$CI_low > 0 | df$CI_high < 0) & df$pd > pd_threshold, "Yes", "No")
  knitr::kable(df[, c("Level1", "Level2", "Difference", "CI_low", "CI_high", "pd", "Credible")], digits = digits)
}

# How many of the 9 condition x age.group cells clear the credibility bar
# (95% CrI excludes zero AND pd > 97.5%). Defined here (see ddm-ai.qmd) since
# the per-parameter Results paragraphs now also quote this count.
count_credible <- function(df, pd_threshold = 0.975) {
  sum((df$CI_low > 0 | df$CI_high < 0) & df$pd > pd_threshold)
}
```

# Results

### Drift Rate

In contrast to advantageous inequity, children distinguish between equal and disadvantageously unequal outcomes from the youngest age tested, and this distinction is evident regardless of prompt condition. At 4–5 years, credible equal-vs.-unequal differences are already present in the autonomous (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "4&5")`), baseline (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "4&5")`), and norm conditions (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "norm", age.group = "4&5")`). This pattern generalizes to the other age groups. Thus, unlike advantageous inequity, explicit fairness framing does not appear necessary for the distinction to emerge. Indeed, at 6–7 years the norm condition shows the smallest effect (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "norm", age.group = "6&7")`), relative to baseline (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "6&7")`) and autonomous (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "6&7")`). This pattern contrasts with advantageous inequity, where the norm condition showed the earliest and strongest differentiation.

Plotted together with `ndt`, `bias`, and `bs` at the end of the Results section (one combined figure via `patchwork`) rather than as four separate figures.

```{r}
#| label: fig-mu
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.5
draws_mu_di <- pairs(emmeans(fit_di, ~ dist | condition * age.group, dpar = "mu")) |>
  gather_emmeans_draws()

p_mu_di <- ggplot(draws_mu_di, aes(x = .value, y = condition, fill = condition)) +
  stat_halfeye() +
  facet_wrap(~age.group) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Difference in drift rate (eq - uneq)", y = "Condition", title = "Drift rate (mu)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14)
```

#### Main Effects

**Age.**

```{r}
kable_means(mu_by_age_di)
kable_contrasts(contrasts_mu_age_di)
```

Drift rate strengthens (grows more negative) credibly from 4–5y to both 6–7y and 8–9y, but the 6–7y-to-8–9y step is `r credible_label(contrasts_mu_age_di, Level1 = "6&7", Level2 = "8&9")` — nearly all of the age-related change happens by 6–7y, consistent with the cell-level result that disadvantageous inequity aversion is already present at the youngest age tested.

**Condition.**

```{r}
kable_means(mu_by_cond_di)
kable_contrasts(contrasts_mu_cond_di)
```

No pairwise condition difference is credible — reinforcing the cell-level finding that framing does not gate this effect the way it does in the AI group.

**Dist.**

```{r}
kable_means(mu_by_dist_di)
kable_contrasts(contrasts_mu_dist_di)
```

Averaged across every condition and age, drift rate is credibly more negative on equal-split trials than unequal-split trials (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_dist_di)`) — the largest marginal `dist` effect of any parameter in either document, consistent with `mu` being credible in all 9 of 9 cells above.

### Non-Decision Time

In contrast to drift rate, non-decision time shows no evidence of a systematic equal-vs.-unequal distinction.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ndt
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.5
draws_ndt_di <- pairs(emmeans(fit_di, ~ dist | condition * age.group, dpar = "ndt")) |>
  gather_emmeans_draws()

p_ndt_di <- ggplot(draws_ndt_di, aes(x = .value, y = condition, fill = condition)) +
  stat_halfeye() +
  facet_wrap(~age.group) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Difference in ndt, seconds (eq - uneq)", y = "Condition", title = "Non-decision time (ndt)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14)
```

#### Main Effects

**Age.**

```{r}
kable_means(ndt_by_age_di)
kable_contrasts(contrasts_ndt_age_di)
```

No pairwise age difference in `ndt` is credible.

**Condition.**

```{r}
kable_means(ndt_by_cond_di)
kable_contrasts(contrasts_ndt_cond_di)
```

No pairwise condition difference in `ndt` is credible either.

**Dist.**

```{r}
kable_means(ndt_by_dist_di)
kable_contrasts(contrasts_ndt_dist_di)
```

The marginal eq-vs-uneq difference in `ndt` is `r credible_label(contrasts_ndt_dist_di)` (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_ndt_dist_di)`). All three main effects agree with the cell-level result: `ndt` carries no locus of the disadvantageous-inequity effect in this group.

### Starting Point (Bias)

One caveat: because children cannot know whether an upcoming trial is equal or unequal before it starts, bias is best understood as a pre-trial setting rather than something that should vary by trial type. A credible equal-vs.-unequal difference here more likely reflects the model absorbing some residual asymmetry between trial types than a literal advance adjustment. Starting-point contrasts are on the natural 0–1 probability scale (matching how `bias` values are reported elsewhere in this document), which is why the plot below applies `regrid("response")` before taking pairwise differences.

Starting-point bias showed a more limited developmental effect. Equal-vs.-unequal differences became credible at 6–7 years in the autonomous (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "6&7")`) and baseline conditions (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "6&7")`) and remained credible at 8–9 years (autonomous: `r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "8&9")`; baseline: `r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "8&9")`). No corresponding effect emerged in the norm condition at any age. Despite these within-condition contrasts, overall starting-point estimates were similar across conditions (autonomous = `r fmt_mean(bias_by_condition_di, condition = "autonomous")`; baseline = `r fmt_mean(bias_by_condition_di, condition = "baseline")`; norm = `r fmt_mean(bias_by_condition_di, condition = "norm")`), indicating that the effect was specific to the equal-versus-unequal distinction rather than a general shift in response bias.

```{r}
#| label: fig-bias
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.5
draws_bias_di <- emmeans(fit_di, ~ dist | condition * age.group, dpar = "bias") |>
  regrid("response") |>
  pairs() |>
  gather_emmeans_draws()

p_bias_di <- ggplot(draws_bias_di, aes(x = .value, y = condition, fill = condition)) +
  stat_halfeye() +
  facet_wrap(~age.group) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Difference in bias, probability scale (eq - uneq)", y = "Condition", title = "Starting point (bias)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14)
```

#### Main Effects

Same scale note as `ddm-ai.qmd`: `bias_by_age_di`/`_cond_di`/`_dist_di` and their contrasts are on the natural (0-1 probability) response scale by default.

**Age.**

```{r}
kable_means(bias_by_age_di)
kable_contrasts(contrasts_bias_age_di)
```

Only 4–5y-vs-8–9y clears the credibility bar (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bias_age_di, Level1 = "4&5", Level2 = "8&9")`), and only just — the same gradual-drift pattern as in the AI document, not a sharp transition.

**Condition.**

```{r}
kable_means(bias_by_condition_di)
kable_contrasts(contrasts_bias_cond_di)
```

No pairwise condition difference is credible, matching the marginal-by-condition means already reported above (no credible difference between conditions).

**Dist.**

```{r}
kable_means(bias_by_dist_di)
kable_contrasts(contrasts_bias_dist_di)
```

Averaged over condition and age, the eq-vs-uneq difference in starting point is credible (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bias_dist_di)`) — consistent with `bias` being this group's real secondary carrier of the effect (autonomous and baseline, from 6–7y onward, per the cell-level results above).

### Boundary Separation

One caveat: boundary separation is conventionally a pre-trial, response-caution setting rather than something that should vary by trial type, so a credible equal-vs.-unequal difference here more likely reflects the model absorbing some residual asymmetry between trial types than children genuinely adjusting caution in advance.

Unlike advantageous inequity, boundary separation shows no reliable pattern in this group.

```{r}
#| label: fig-bs
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.5
draws_bs_di <- pairs(emmeans(fit_di, ~ dist | condition * age.group, dpar = "bs")) |>
  gather_emmeans_draws()

p_bs_di <- ggplot(draws_bs_di, aes(x = .value, y = condition, fill = condition)) +
  stat_halfeye() +
  facet_wrap(~age.group) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Difference in bs (eq - uneq)", y = "Condition", title = "Boundary separation (bs)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14)
```

#### Main Effects

**Age.**

```{r}
kable_means(bs_by_age_di)
kable_contrasts(contrasts_bs_age_di)
```

No pairwise age difference is credible — unlike AI, where the oldest group pulled credibly ahead of the middle group.

**Condition.**

```{r}
kable_means(bs_by_condition_di)
kable_contrasts(contrasts_bs_cond_di)
```

No pairwise condition difference is credible either, consistent with the marginal-by-condition means already reported above.

**Dist.**

```{r}
kable_means(bs_by_dist_di)
kable_contrasts(contrasts_bs_dist_di)
```

The marginal eq-vs-uneq difference in `bs` is `r credible_label(contrasts_bs_dist_di)` (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bs_dist_di)`) — worth flagging a tension with the cell-level result above, where only 2 of 9 cells cleared the credibility bar individually. Pooling over condition and age recovers a consistent-enough direction (wider boundaries on equal-split trials, same sign as every credible cell) for the *marginal* effect to reach credibility even though most individual cells, taken alone, do not. This is a real but diffuse signal, not the coherent condition-specific pattern AI shows.

### Combined figure

```{r}
#| label: fig-combined
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 21
p_mu_di / p_ndt_di / p_bias_di / p_bs_di
```

For context, the marginal bias per condition (averaged over `dist`/`age.group`), on the natural (0, 1) scale: autonomous `r fmt_mean(bias_by_condition_di, condition = "autonomous")`, baseline `r fmt_mean(bias_by_condition_di, condition = "baseline")`, norm `r fmt_mean(bias_by_condition_di, condition = "norm")`.

```{r}
ggplot(draws_bias_marginal_di, aes(x = .value, y = condition, fill = condition)) +
```

For context, the marginal boundary separation per condition (averaged over `dist`/`age.group`): autonomous `r fmt_mean(bs_by_condition_di, condition = "autonomous")`, baseline `r fmt_mean(bs_by_condition_di, condition = "baseline")`, norm `r fmt_mean(bs_by_condition_di, condition = "norm")`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-bs-marginal
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
draws_bs_marginal_di <- emmeans(fit_di, ~condition, dpar = "bs") |>
  gather_emmeans_draws()

ggplot(draws_bs_marginal_di, aes(x = .value, y = condition, fill = condition)) +
  stat_halfeye() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Boundary separation (bs)", y = "Condition", title = "DI: bs by condition (marginal over dist, age.group)") +
```

## Summary

Credibility throughout is based on the 95% credible interval excluding zero together with `pd > 97.5%` (`count_credible()`, defined in the formatters chunk above).

Taken together, disadvantageous inequity aversion is present from the youngest age tested and is largely independent of experimental framing, with the effect concentrated in drift rate: the `dist` contrast reaches credibility in `r count_credible(contrasts_mu_di)` of 9 cells for drift rate, versus `r count_credible(contrasts_ndt_di)` of 9 for `ndt`, `r count_credible(contrasts_bias_di)` of 9 for bias, and `r count_credible(contrasts_bs_di)` of 9 for boundary separation. This matches the source paper's own finding that the Prompt x Allocation x Age interaction was dropped for disadvantageous inequity because it did not improve model fit. Starting-point bias shows a secondary role specific to the autonomous and baseline conditions, emerging from 6–7 years onward and absent when children were explicitly prompted to be fair — the opposite pattern from advantageous inequity, where boundary separation, not starting point, carried the secondary effect, and specifically in the norm condition. This is the mirror image of the AI document's conclusion, where the fairness prompt was necessary to unlock early, credible inequity aversion: normative framing shapes children's willingness to reject advantageous (self-benefiting) unfairness, but disadvantageous inequity aversion does not need that kind of external prompting to show up early.
